name: Pain de mie

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use water chilled to about 5°C and reduce it by 10 g (mL).

steps.title: Prepare the pan and ingredients
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade firmly on the clean mounting shaft. Add only the initial bread-pan flour and other ingredients in a mound (exclude yeast, all dispenser additions and all ingredients reserved for later) in the centre of the bread pan; pour the water around the edges. Fit and lock the pan in the appliance. Put the yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Close both lids securely. (Manual p. 18.)

steps.title: Set and start the machine
steps.text: Select program 1, then press Start. Do not open the lid after starting except at a documented manual-addition step.

steps.title: Remove and cool
steps.text: When the machine beeps at completion, press Cancel and unplug. Use dry oven mitts to remove the hot bread pan. Set it on a cloth-covered surface and cool for about 2 minutes, then remove the bread onto a raised wire rack. Check for the kneading blade before cutting. Do not use a knife, fork or chopsticks or touch the underside of the pan. (Manual pp. 18–19.)

notes: At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use water chilled to about 5°C and reduce it by 10 g (mL).
Timer availability is subject to the recipe ingredients and the restrictions on manual pp. 20 and 24; this companion does not choose a delayed start.

steps.text: At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove hot pan with dry oven mitts; cool about 2 minutes then remove gently. Check for blade. Vigorous shaking can damage shape. If Cancel has not been pressed, set time then Start. Hold Cancel to stop.

notes: Scrape flour after about 7 minutes (p. 10).

Some rice flour contains gluten. If you have a wheat allergy, check ingredients. Contact flour manufacturer if allergic symptoms develop. Result resembles butter cake, not commercial sponge cake; crust will be dark.
If 15 minutes elapse at scraping, the program resumes automatically.
If Cancel is pressed accidentally at an intervention, press Start within 10 minutes to resume (once only; pressing another key disables this).
The manual lists this addition under rice flour cake variations; use the original ingredient order.

name: Mugwort mochi (2 go)

ingredients.name: Dusting starch (potato starch, non-glutinous rice flour or cornstarch)

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: Do not soak rice; soaking makes mochi too soft. If accidentally soaked, suggested water reduction: 2 go 80 g (mL); 3 go 140 g (mL). The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Rinse and drain
steps.text: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Do not soak. Drain in colander 30 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare and start
steps.text: Fit noodle/mochi blade. Add rice then water. Fit pan. Select program 36 and press Start.

steps.title: Open lid at machine beep
steps.text: At about 50 or 55 minutes (p. 10), open lid. Do not press Cancel. Leave lid open and press Start immediately to release excess moisture. If 30 minutes elapse pounding starts automatically with lid closed.

steps.title: Add during pounding
steps.text: Boil mugwort leaves, soak in cold water to remove bitterness, chop finely and squeeze well. Once pounding starts, gradually add the variation ingredients.

steps.title: Remove and shape
steps.text: Use dry oven mitts for the hot pan; do not touch hot parts (manual pp. 4–5). At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove pan immediately and cool until touchable (5–10 minutes). Lift mochi from underneath onto heat-resistant tray dusted with starch. Pinch and roll portions. Wet hands to eat immediately; starch hands for storage. Alternatively wrap directly in plastic wrap and cut into blocks.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Cool and brush off excess starch. Keep in cool dry place up to 2 days, or double-bag sealed in freezer up to one month.

notes: Do not soak rice; soaking makes mochi too soft. If accidentally soaked, suggested water reduction: 2 go 80 g (mL); 3 go 140 g (mL).
Do not add hard ingredients such as beans; they can peel pan coating.
Boil mugwort leaves, soak in cold water to remove bitterness, chop finely and squeeze well.
The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).
otherTime: Drain 30 min before cycle; cool 5–10 min after cycle. Shaping time unspecified.

steps.title: Prepare the pan and ingredients
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade firmly on the clean mounting shaft. Add only the initial bread-pan flour and other ingredients in a mound (exclude yeast, all dispenser additions and all ingredients reserved for later) in the centre of the bread pan; pour the water around the edges. Fit and lock the pan in the appliance. Put the yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Close both lids securely. (Manual p. 18.)

steps.title: Set and start the machine
steps.text: Select program 9, then press Start. Do not open the lid after starting except at a documented manual-addition step.

steps.title: Remove and cool
steps.text: When the machine beeps at completion, press Cancel and unplug. Use dry oven mitts to remove the hot bread pan. Set it on a cloth-covered surface and cool for about 2 minutes, then remove the bread onto a raised wire rack. Check for the kneading blade before cutting. Do not use a knife, fork or chopsticks or touch the underside of the pan. (Manual pp. 18–19.)

notes: At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use water chilled to about 5°C and reduce it by 10 g (mL).
